This page is written according to the U.S. O*NET-SOC 47-1011.00 “First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers” (the fixed index assigns this asset the Chinese occupational name for this occupation, and the body text follows that official occupational scope). Even within on-site supervision, the differences are large: housing construction and structures, municipal and infrastructure work, roads and bridges, industrial plants and equipment installation, specialty subcontractor coordination, and extraction operations such as mining and quarrying; a supervisor may lead only one crew or coordinate several trades and subcontractors at once. Before comparing positions or development paths, first check: the education and professional qualifications required for the role, whether special operations or work-at-height qualifications are required, on-site safety training and personal protection requirements, working hours and overtime arrangements, and whether mobility among multiple sites is required.

Validate with one paper exercise: you are given a completely fictitious construction assignment (project type and scale, the work items to be completed, drawing and specification key points, available personnel and equipment, material delivery schedules, and the available weather and schedule window). You are asked to write out the pre-start check points, crew assignments and work sequence, progress and quality control points, safety and protection requirements, the requisition and deployment plan for materials and equipment, whom to coordinate with, and to mark which decisions must be made by the project manager or personnel with the corresponding qualifications.

Signals worth considering more: willingness to work outdoors and on site over the long term, ability to verify details against drawings and specifications, and ability to coordinate amid multiple overlapping trades and put safety before schedule. Signals requiring caution: unwillingness to work on site and outdoors over the long term, difficulty holding to safety and quality procedures under schedule pressure, and imagining on-site management as only reading reports in an office.
This card is a career exploration reference and does not constitute hiring, ability scoring, safety, or practice conclusions.

First judge whether you are willing to make the supervision of on-site construction and extraction work a long-term career: it requires working outdoors and on site over the long term, verifying quality and safety against drawings and specifications, organizing crews and subcontractors to advance in sequence, and bearing supervisory responsibility for the safety of personnel working on the same site; validate with the paper exercise and seven-day task on this page.

The work of first-line supervisors of construction trades and extraction workers revolves around the cycle of “pre-start preparation—assignment and scheduling—process supervision—coordination and changes—acceptance and records”: before starting, verify drawings, specifications, and permits, check that personnel, equipment, and materials are in place, and complete the safety briefing; arrange crew assignments and the work sequence by work item and specify progress and quality control points; during construction, patrol the site and verify that dimensions, elevations, and methods conform to the drawings and specifications, check safety protection and working conditions, and correct and record deviations promptly; coordinate the arrival sequence of different trades, subcontractors, and materials and equipment, handle on-site changes and unexpected problems, and report upward within authorization; after each work item is completed, organize self-inspection and acceptance, organize progress, quality, safety, and material records, take part in training and mentoring, and report to the project manager. The emphasis differs greatly by direction: housing and structural work stresses crew organization and trade sequencing, municipal and infrastructure work stresses overlapping operations and underground utilities, industrial and equipment installation work stresses precision and inspection lots, extraction work stresses specialty safety such as slopes and blasting, and specialty subcontract management stresses contract interfaces and schedule coordination.
U.S. O*NET-SOC 47-1011.00 “First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers”: directly supervise and coordinate the work of construction or extraction workers.

Main objects | Construction drawings and specifications, crew and subcontractor workers, engineering materials and components, construction machinery and hand tools, on-site safety protection facilities, and progress and quality records.

Record requirements | Pre-shift check and safety briefing records, construction logs and progress records, quality inspection and acceptance records, material arrival and inspection records, and hazard rectification and accident report records must be kept on file according to institutional rules.

Environment and pace | The site presents risks of work at heights, machinery injury, noise and dust, underground utilities, and extraction slopes; schedules and weather have an obvious impact, and during schedule crunches the work intensity is concentrated and overtime is required.

subject.name: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
subject.summary: Directly supervise and coordinate the work of construction or extraction workers: includes checking construction progress and quality against drawings and specifications, supervising work safety and personal protection, arranging crew assignments and trade sequencing, estimating materials and labor hours and requisitioning materials and equipment, coordinating the work sequence among different trades and subcontractors, organizing training and mentoring, and recording progress and deviations and reporting to superiors.
